topic: Major Fairs and Festivals of Uttar Pradesh (State Specific GK)
description: A comprehensive study guide covering the vibrant and culturally rich fairs and festivals of Uttar Pradesh. This topic is highly crucial for state-level competitive exams, especially for 'match the following' and direct location-based questions.

sections.title: Kumbh and Magh Mela
sections.description: The world's largest religious gatherings held at the confluence of sacred rivers in Prayagraj.

key_concepts.explanation: Organized every 12 years in Prayagraj at the Triveni Sangam (confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati). It is recognized as the largest peaceful gathering of people in the world.
Organized every 6 years in Prayagraj, marking the halfway point between two Maha Kumbh Melas.
An annual fair held on the banks of the Sangam in Prayagraj during the Hindu month of Magh (January-February).

historical_events.significance: The Kumbh Mela was officially inscribed on the UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

sections.title: Major Regional Fairs
sections.description: Prominent fairs held in specific districts of Uttar Pradesh that are frequently asked in exams.

key_associations.extra_info: A renowned symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity, held simultaneously at the Navchandi Temple and the shrine of the Sufi saint Bale Miyan.
A massive animal and cattle fair organized on the banks of the Yamuna River, highly famous for the trading of camels.
An annual fair held at the holy shrine (dargah) of the revered Sufi saint Haji Waris Ali Shah.
A famous annual fair organized at the Dargah of the warrior saint Syed Salar Masood Ghazi.
A prominent fair held during the Navratri festival at the Shakumbhari Devi Shakti Peeth.

sections.title: Religious and Cultural Festivals
sections.description: Crucial festivals dedicated to various deities, historical figures, and the promotion of regional art and culture.

key_associations.extra_info: A unique and globally famous celebration of Holi in the month of Phalguna, where women playfully beat men with sticks (lathis).
A 10-day annual cultural extravaganza held at Shilpgram, promoting traditional Indian art, crafts, culture, and cuisine.
One of the biggest annual events in North India, featuring a grand reenactment of the marriage procession of Lord Rama.
Celebrated during Dev Deepawali, where the majestic ghats of the river Ganga are illuminated with millions of earthen lamps.
Organized at the Samadhi Sthal of the great mystic poet and saint Kabirdas to commemorate his life, philosophy, and teachings.

sections.title: Other Important Fairs
sections.description: Additional notable fairs that frequently appear in 'match the following' type questions.

key_associations.extra_info: Considered to be the second largest cattle fair in India, held annually on Kartik Purnima.
A widely attended regional fair held in the memory of Baba Govind Sahab.
A religious fair organized in the holy month of Shravan to honor Lord Shiva at the Kailash Temple.
A spiritual gathering where devotees perform the circumambulation (Parikrama) of these holy cities.

sections.title: Important Facts
sections.description: Crucial statistical and geographical one-liner facts related to the fairs and festivals of Uttar Pradesh.

important_facts.fact: The maximum number of fairs in Uttar Pradesh are held in the Mathura district (approximately 86 fairs annually).
The minimum number of fairs in Uttar Pradesh are held in the Kanpur and Hamirpur districts.
The Swami Haridas Jayanti Mela is held annually in Vrindavan (Mathura) to honor the legendary classical musician and saint Swami Haridas.
